messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert triggered — service=auth-service severity=critical — symptom=JWT verification failures (401 spike) across hosted and dedicated. PD: https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PD12345

pagerduty: Incident PD12345 created and paged OnCall-SRE. Primary: emily.ops. Escalation policy: auth-rotation-policy.

emily.ops: ack — looking now. Paging oliver-sre and sanjay.eng for JWKS/rotation context.

oliver-sre: on it. I'm seeing a flood of 401s with error "kid not found in JWKS" in auth-prod logs. Pattern started ~03:14 UTC.

sanjay.eng: I can confirm. Automated key rotation kicked at 03:13:48 UTC and looks like the signing service published new kid before the JWKS cache propagated to verifiers. Some tokens signed with new kid aren't verifiable.

leah-support: CS reports multiple integrations failing to authenticate. Topline: ~18-25% of requests across mobile SDKs and some server-to-server clients are returning 401. Customers reporting token invalidation errors.

emily.ops: mitigation plan (immediate):
1) Force JWKS cache invalidation across all auth nodes.
2) Re-publish previous signing key to JWKS endpoint as a fallback.
3) Temporarily accept tokens signed by either kid for verification (10m window).
4) Notify customers and update status page.

oliver-sre: I'm invalidating caches now. Running a rolling command to clear local JWKS caches on auth pods.

```bash
# rolling invalidate
for host in $(cat /opt/redwood/auth_hosts.txt); do
  ssh $host 'curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/internal/keys/invalidate && echo "cleared $host"'
done
```

oliver-sre: cache invalidation in progress — 30% hosts cleared, seeing drop in 401s on those hosts in metrics.

sanjay.eng: prepping a quick JWKS patch to re-include old key (re-publish). Applying k8s patch to jwks-service now.

```yaml
# k8s patch (canary)
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: jwks-keys
data:
  keys.json: |
    [
      {"kid":"old-kid", "kty":"RSA", "n":"...", "e":"AQAB"},
      {"kid":"new-kid", "kty":"RSA", "n":"...", "e":"AQAB"}
    ]
```

sanjay.eng: patch deployed to canary, verifying.

incident-bot: emily.ops acknowledged the page.

emily.ops: I'm enabling dual-kid acceptance in the verifier config for a 10m window while we stabilize. Will revert after confirmation.

oliver-sre: dual-kid toggle applied on canary nodes. Verification errors dropped from 22% -> 4% on canary. Rolling to remaining nodes.

leah-support: CS update: notified top 10 customers via email + posted draft on status page (waiting for emily to approve wording). Customers reporting partial recovery, a few still need token refresh.

oliver-sre: rolling cache invalidation completed. All hosts show the new jwks payload (includes both keys). 401 rate now ~1.5% and trending down.

sanjay.eng: full JWKS patch is live. We're monitoring for any residual verification failures. Canaries look healthy.

emily.ops: great work. Next steps for post-incident:
- Create incident ticket with timeline and root cause
- Add a blocking check in rotation script to wait for JWKS propagation and successful verifier fetch on at least 90% of nodes before completing rotation
- Add automatic JWKS refetch if 4xx auth spike detected
- Run a tabletop rotation drill next week

leah-support: status page update approved and published. Customers acknowledged recovery; one enterprise reported they needed to regenerate client tokens (we assisted).

incident-bot: PagerDuty incident PD12345 resolved by emily.ops — status: resolved.

emily.ops: closing thread. I'll follow up with a full postmortem doc and action owners. Thanks everyone. :heart:
